lines.text: Many learners say: I need a morning call at six.
Better: I need a wake-up call at six.
A wake-up call wakes you up.
Wake-up! I need a wake-up call at six.

data.wrong: I need a morning call at six.
data.right: I need a wake-up call at six.
data.why: A wake-up call wakes you up.

en.tip: “Morning call” is not English. Say wake-up call. Say “I need a wake-up call at six.”
en.caption: Do you say “I need a morning call at six” in English? 😅 Morning call is not used in English, so say wake-up call! “I need a wake-up call at six” is right. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
